**Rb7+** - moving the rook from a7 to b7 with check.

This forces Black's king:

After **1. Rb7+ Ka5**, White has **2. Ra6#** - checkmate! The king on a5 has no escape (a4 and b5 controlled by the rook on a6, b6 controlled by the rook on b7, b4 blocked by Black's own rook).

**Coaching note:**
When your opponent's king is driven into the open, look for forcing moves to push it further into danger. Here, a rook check drives the king to the edge of the board where it becomes trapped. Always calculate checks and captures completely—this position had a forced two-move mate that wins the game immediately.
